correctness.rationale: Self-contained induction establishes complete-alphabet arch iff universality. A palindrome requires paired letter multiplicities except for its center. Sharp lower bounds are reached by explicit mirrored permutations. For odd k, simultaneous left/right greedy arch boundaries sandwich a full-alphabet central block, and equality forces each outer arch to be a permutation and the center to have exactly \(2q-1\) symbols. Unique parsing gives the factorial count. Every hypothesis \(q\ge2\), \(k\ge1\) and parity case, including k=1, is treated. Independent exhaustive direct-subsequence checker passes all stated finite domains but is not used as an infinite proof.

value.rationale: The restricted shortest common-supersequence problem for the complete language \(\Sigma^k\) has a natural reversal-symmetry constraint. Unlike a renamed unconstrained \(qk\) theorem, the answer exhibits a sharp parity-dependent q-1 length penalty, a forced minimal all-symbol central palindrome, a complete infinite two-parameter classification of all extremal words, and their exact labeled count. This provides optimal reversible sequence templates with deterministic shape and enumeration; no unsupported downstream theorem or practical performance is claimed.
